q: What are the embedded emissions of ferrochrome or ferromanganese per tonne under CBAM?
title: Ferrochrome and ferromanganese CBAM CO2
short: Ferrochrome and ferromanganese fall under CBAM as iron and steel goods, so only direct emissions count: mainly the CO2 from coke, coal and electrode paste used as reductants, worked out by carbon mass balance. Smelter electricity is not charged. Without your own verified data, the importer uses the default value for the CN code.
audience: Ferroalloy producers (Odisha, Andhra Pradesh), EU importers

p: Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 lists CN heading 7202 under iron and steel, but excludes several subheadings by name. Ferromanganese (7202 11, 7202 19), ferrochromium (7202 41, 7202 49) and ferronickel (7202 60) are in. Ferrosilicon, ferro-silico-manganese and ferro-silico-chromium are among the exclusions, so a silicomanganese plant should check its exact 8-digit code before doing any CBAM work.

sections.h: The mass balance for direct emissions
p: CO2 = (carbon in all reductants and electrode paste minus carbon leaving in the alloy, slag and dust) x 44/12. Each input is tonnes used in the period times its carbon content from the supplier analysis or your lab. Add CO2 from fuel burnt in preheaters, ladle heating or sinter and pellet plants inside the installation, and from carbonate fluxes if you use them.

For iron and steel goods the definitive period counts direct emissions only. A submerged arc furnace uses a lot of electricity per tonne, but that indirect CO2 is not charged, even from a captive power plant. Keep the electricity figure anyway: EU buyers often want the full footprint, and the Commission is required to assess extending indirect emissions to more goods.

ul: Default values are set by CN code and country in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, with a mark-up that rises each year.
Reported actual emissions, monitored by the installation operator and verified, usually cost the importer less than defaults when your reductant use is efficient.
Ferroalloys made with high-carbon reductants and little carbon in the product sit at the top of the range, so compare your mass balance with the default before choosing.

example.title: Illustrative mass balance for one tonne of high-carbon ferrochrome
lines: Metallurgical coke: 550 kg x 85% carbon = 467.5 kg C
Electrode paste: 25 kg x 85% carbon = 21.25 kg C
Carbon in the alloy: 1,000 kg x 7% = 70 kg C; carbon in slag assumed negligible
Direct CO2: 418.75 x 44/12 = 1,535 kg, about 1.54 t CO2 per tonne of alloy
Not counted for CBAM: 3,800 kWh x 0.710 = 2,698 kg CO2 from grid electricity
example.note: Inputs and carbon contents are assumed for illustration. Use measured consumption and analyses for your furnace, and add any fuel combustion inside the installation.
